text:
sam: Heads-up: us-west-4 dedicated pool at 98% GPU allocation (H100s). We're seeing queuing on low-priority orgs and eviction spikes. Putting pool into lameduck-weighted-drain to avoid hard evictions. Moving non-prod tenants to hosted with staged weights.
joel: ack. Can you post the current pool metrics? CPU/GPU/mem + queue depth?
sam: GPU util 98%, available gpus 2/128, preemption rate up 12% in the last 5m, p99 latency climbing from 80ms->220ms, backlog ~430 requests.
ada: (typo) ada: thanks. Which tenant groups are targeted for move? We need to protect dedicated SLA customers.
sam: Targeting: low-priority orgs (tag: burstable), ci/cd, internal-batch. Not touching reserved customers pinned to pool. Weight changes: decrease dedicated weight for burstable from 0.18->0.03 over 10min; increase hosted from 0.02->0.17.
lina: Can we do a staged warmup on hosted side to avoid cold KV cache misses? Last time we saw token cost spike.
joel: yes — plan: 1) route 10% of shifted traffic to hosted with warmup header to populate prefix cache; 2) monitor error rates and token cost; 3) ramp to final weight over 10m.
matt: I'll open a quick canary with the routing service. Command I run: `./routerctl set-weight --region us-west-4 --from dedicated --to hosted --tenant-group burstable --step 0.1 --interval 60s --warmup true`
sam: ops-bot will trigger the automation once we confirm. ops-bot: please validate canary config.
ops-bot: automation check OK. Canary plan validated. No conflicting rollouts in region.
ada: we should also set temporary lower model quality for these groups to cut GPU memory per request (switch to quantized variant). That lowers perf cost and helps fit.
joel: agreed. We'll route burstable to model: redwood/open-llm-h100-quantized:v2 for non-prod. Reserved customers remain on full variant.
lina: timeline? If things don't stabilize, we'll need to force-failover all burstable -> hosted and enable eviction policy.
sam: start canary now. I'll watch dashboard and handle org notifications for rate limits.
(2 minutes later)
joel: canary metrics: first 10% traffic to hosted shows p95 latency +40ms, error rate 0.1% (within threshold), token cost +12% for canary. KV warmup metrics show steady prefix hits after ~90s.
matt: continuing to ramp to 30% now.
(8 minutes later)
joel: at 30% ramp, dedicated pool freed ~18 gpus, queue depth down to 120, preemption rate back to baseline 1.4%. p99 steady at 95ms.
sam: good. Keep the staged ramp. After full shift complete, we plan to spin up small ephemeral nodes to avoid repeated drains overnight.
lina: action items: - matt to finish weight ramp - joel to verify no SLA customers impacted - ada to run cost delta calc for shift - sam to open post-incident note if we end up evicting any reserved workloads
ada: cost delta: preliminary estimate +11% token cost for moved workloads during warmup window, but net savings vs emergency scale-up.
sam: notes for follow-up: check autoscaler thresholds for us-west-4, consider raising soft-limit by 10% for H100 pools, and add routing rule to prefer nearby regions before hosted for low-latency reserved cases.
matt: done — completed ramp to target weights. Monitoring for 10m stabilization window.
(20 minutes later)
joel: stabilization OK. No reservation evictions. Pool util now 65%. We'll keep lameduck-weighted-drain in place for 1hr then reassess.
sam: thanks team. I'll file a short incident blurb and schedule a postmortem if we see recurrence. :thumbsup:
